subject: NashCap: Request to accelerate SLA/controls work for contract close
messages:
From: Lydia Park <l.park@nashcap.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production requirements and contract timeline

Karthik — thanks again for the demo last week. NashCap's procurement team is requesting a clear delivery plan for the following items before legal will sign: 

- Per-tenant control over prompt-caching (ability to disable/enable at tenant level)
- Transparent 95th-percentile latency SLO for our top route (fraud-detection pipeline)
- Ability to pin model variants for a subset of traffic for deterministic outputs during closed beta

We are planning to sign in early December but procurement says these items need an explicit acceptance/commit in our SOW or they will push the timeline. Can your team confirm feasibility and a rough timeline? I attached our high-level risk summary (separate file).

Thanks,
Lydia
VP Product, NashCap

Attachment: NashCap_Risk_Summary.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Product Team <product@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Nov 2028 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Production requirements and contract timeline

Team — forwarding NashCap's note. They are a high-velocity mid-enterprise prospect; likely $600k ARR first year if we can close in this quarter. Procurement insists on three items being explicitly covered in the SOW (see Lydia's list).

Ask: can Eng/Product evaluate scope and provide a yes/no on moving any of these into an "activation exception" or a short-term engineering commitment tied to the contract? If we can't commit, they said they'll push signing to next quarter. 

Quick context: NashCap will run a fraud-detection route that is latency-sensitive and steady-state request volume is modest (<200 reqs/min) but tail matters. They specifically called out tenant-level prompt-caching controls (they want ability to turn caching off for PCI/payment prompts), a firm 95th P99 latency SLO for the route, and a model-pinning option during a closed beta.

I appreciate quick flags — procurement is asking for language by EOD Monday.

—Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Product Team <product@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Nov 2028 08:28:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production requirements and contract timeline

Adding customer context: NashCap handles both PCI-adjacent prompts and sensitive identity graphs. Their legal team is explicit: they will accept a contractual commitment if we either (A) provide per-tenant control to disable prompt caching + audit logs showing caching state per request, or (B) offer a demonstrable operational control in our console plus an SLA note that penalties apply if cache control can't be honored during pilot.

Commercial note: they are negotiating a 12-month committed seat with an option to expand. If we push the timeline they may seek a competitor with similar low-latency guarantees. I recommend we consider a scoped, limited-time feature flag rather than a long-term platform change to reduce risk.

I'll join whatever sync is needed to align wording for SOW/SoA.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Customer Success — Strategic Accounts

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Nov 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production requirements and contract timeline

Thanks — quick technical read. High-level feasibility:

- Per-tenant prompt-caching toggle: small infra surface (config + runtime check) but we need to validate migration of existing prefix cache keys. I estimate a 3-week scoped sprint (incl. QA) for a limited admin toggle and request-level audit events. Full UI for customer self-service would be additional.
- 95th PCT latency SLO: we already report P95/P99 across routes, but guaranteeing it contractually will require a runbook (fallback policy, dedicated warm-pool options, and penalty language). To confidently commit we need to map NashCap's projected qps distribution and confirm no cross-tenant noisy-neighbor risk. Engineering effort to add per-route SLO enforcement + alerting: ~2 sprints to instrument and validate with canary.
- Model-pinning for closed beta: we support model variants but guaranteeing residency/affinity needs scheduler work; however we can offer a beta policy where we route a fixed percentage of traffic to a pinned variant with explicit rollback controls. Scoped implementation: 2 weeks if limited to routing rules, 5+ weeks for affinity guarantees.

Questions for sales/CS to answer (quick):
1) What is projected qps for the fraud route in peak (reqs/min)?
2) Do they require customer self-service UI or is a managed toggle OK for the pilot?
3) What contractual SLO delta do they expect (P95 target number)?

If procurement needs explicit SOW language by Monday, we can offer a conditional commitment: "Redwood will deliver a scoped prompt-cache toggle and per-route SLO instrumentation within X weeks from contract signature, subject to capacity validation." That would buy time while we scope the full UI/work.

I can carve out a small squad for the initial sprint if Product OKs priority. Need Product/Eng prioritization ticket and business decision to treat this as an activation exception.

—Irene
Senior PM, Runtime Reliability

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 16:48:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production requirements and contract timeline

Appreciate the breakdown — this is exactly the level we need. NashCap answered the qps question this morning: peak fraud route is projected at 300 reqs/min with bursts to 700 for short windows. They confirmed that a managed toggle for the pilot is acceptable, and their legal accepted conditional SOW language.

Attached: NashCap_MutualActionPlan_v3.pdf (PDF stub), NashCap_SOW_draft.docx (docx stub). Procurement requested the following SOW snippet (we can refine):

"Redwood will deliver a scoped, operator-managed per-tenant prompt-caching disable and per-route instrumentation to support P95 reporting within 21 calendar days of contract execution. Any production SLO commitments will be subject to capacity validation and may require a short-term dedicated warm pool; details to be agreed during onboarding."

Requesting: Product sign-off to treat this as an activation exception and productize the scoped sprint (Irene — please confirm team capacity). Legal wants the SOW language by EOD Wednesday to keep signing on track. If Product can greenlight this as a limited-scope exception, I'll lock the deal and coordinate procurement.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: NashCap_MutualActionPlan_v3.pdf, NashCap_SOW_draft.docx
